answer: Escrowed bonds and a referral graph stop bulk fakes. An agent locks 200 units and names a sponsor; all links stay public, so a fake cluster shows. Peers can dispute a suspect: a confirmed fake loses its bond and its sponsor is slashed. A quill-signed cipher proof ties each claim to one key, blocking clone replay, and a comet-burst triggers review. Forging 1,000 identities costs 200,000 units; an honest agent pays 200 once for undiluted rewards.
